blocks.prompt: 6. A vehicle moving with a speed of 36 km/h is stopped by applying brakes and comes to rest in 10 seconds. Find the retardation and distance covered during this time.
blocks.explanation:
Uniform braking means constant acceleration, so the equations of motion apply.
Given: u = 36 km/h, v = 0, t = 10 s. To find: retardation and distance.
Plan: change km/h to m/s, then v = u + at for a, and x = ut + at^2/2 for x.
steps:
Given: \(u = 36\) km/h, \(v = 0\) (comes to rest), \(t = 10\) s.
To find: the retardation and the distance \(x\).
Method: the equations of motion with constant acceleration (7.1.6): \(v = u + at\), \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\). The time is in seconds, so the speed must first be in m/s.

Change the speed to m/s
\[u = 36 \times \dfrac{1000}{3600}\]
\[= 36 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 10\text{ m/s}\]
Why: 1 km = 1000 m and 1 h = 3600 s, so 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s.

Acceleration from \(v = u + at\)
\[0 = 10 + a(10)\]
\[a = -1\text{ m/s}^2\]
Why: this equation links u, v, a and t, and only a is unknown. The minus sign shows the velocity is decreasing: a retardation of 1 m/s^2.

Distance from \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\)
\[x = 10(10) + \tfrac{1}{2}(-1)(10)^2\]
\[= 100 - 50 = 50\text{ m}\]
Why: now u, a and t are all known. The vehicle moves in one direction only, so this displacement is also the distance.

Check with \(2ax = v^2 - u^2\)
\[2(-1)(50) = -100\]
\[0^2 - 10^2 = -100 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the third equation of motion agrees. Also, the area of the triangle under the velocity-time graph is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 10 = 50\).
blocks.final_answer: Retardation \(= 1\) m/s\(^2\) (i.e. \(a = -1\) m/s\(^2\)); distance covered \(= 50\) m
